Associated software and numerical results: LatentBridge version 0.1.0 (commit b11491d4d729ac13870e4e443796e57509e75674). Original software is MIT licensed. This manuscript and its source files are CC BY 4.0. This is a preprint, not a peer-reviewed publication. Generative AI tools, including OpenAI Codex and other language-model assistants, substantially assisted research planning, experimental and analysis code development, literature organization, and manuscript drafting and revision. The author retains responsibility for the scientific content, verification of results and references, and the final manuscript.

item.title: Artificial Intelligence Assisted Lifestyle Counseling in Preventive Cardiology a Clinician in the Loop Perspective
item.description:
[预印本] Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
Lifestyle counseling is central to cardiovascular prevention, yet recommendations may be difficult to communicate within routine consultations and to translate into feasible daily actions. This perspective proposes a clinician supervised framework in which artificial intelligence helps draft patient readable lifestyle plans from explicitly approved clinical instructions. The framework separates deterministic safety rules and curated clinical content from language generation; a template system without machine learning is recognized as a valid alternative. Personalization is limited to clinician verified information and patient stated preferences, including language, food affordability, and practical access to physical activity. Proposed safeguards include data minimization, version controlled source material, documented review, patient clarification, and escalation when inputs are incomplete or conflicting. Particular attention is given to professional accountability, health literacy, digital exclusion, and the possibility that fluent drafts encourage superficial verification. Lifestyle advice is not assumed to be inherently safe, especially in patients with multimorbidity. This article presents a conceptual proposal rather than an evaluated intervention or systematic review. A staged research agenda compares the approach with high quality nonautomated counseling materials and measures safety, comprehension, clinician workload, equity, and sustained behavior change. Any benefit remains to be established empirically; the intended contribution is a testable model of accountable health communication rather than a claim of improved cardiovascular outcomes.

item.title: Machine Learning: A Taxonomy and Research Roadmap
item.description:
[预印本] Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
This technical report presents a comprehensive taxonomy of machine learning methods and a structured roadmap for understanding the field. It organizes machine learning into major learning paradigms, model families, computational mechanisms, task formulations, and deployed systems. The report covers supervised, unsupervised, and semi-supervised learning, probabilistic and statistical learning, kernel methods, ensemble methods, reinforcement learning, optimization, and causal inference. By providing a systematic classification of these approaches and their relationships, the report aims to support students, researchers, and practitioners in navigating the machine learning landscape and identifying directions for further study and research.

item.title: USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TOOLS IN ENGLISH LANGUAGE TEACHING: DIDACTIC OPPORTUNITIES, METHODOLOGICAL APPROACHES, AND EXISTING PROBLEMS
item.description:
[预印本] Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
This article examines the didactic potential, methodological foundations, and practical challenges of using artificial intelligence in English language teaching. It discusses generative AI, intelligent chatbots, automated writing feedback systems, speech recognition technologies, and adaptive learning platforms as tools for developing learners’ communicative competence.

item.title: The Volcanic Engine: Volcanism as Planetary Infrastructure
item.description:
[预印本] Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
Working paper / critical narrative synthesis. Not peer reviewed. Volcanism should be understood as planetary infrastructure: a means by which internal activity supplies and renews surface environments, as well as a source of acute hazard. This paper argues that explaining Earth's long-term habitability requires placing volcanic processes within a coupled interior–surface system. Geological carbon cycling supplies the strongest mechanism, while stagnant-lid models, Venus, and the Lost City ecosystem distinguish supported mechanisms from universal necessity claims. The framework organizes the argument around supply, transformation, removal, and response time. This is a selective synthesis of published literature; it reports no new measurements, simulations, or independent model replications. Version 1.0 corrects and substantially revises the earlier web essay, including its claims about subduction, volatile delivery, extinction causation, and direct access to magma. Related book: The Volcanic Engine: Living on a Firing Planet, Book 6 of The Maha Research Series, by Mayone Maha Rajan. Book information · Kindle edition. Purchase is not required to evaluate the paper. Educational companion: Mayon Volcano offers elevation-based 3D exploration and illustrations of volcanic processes. iOS/iPadOS · Android · Web resource. Features vary by platform and version. It is not a monitoring, forecasting, warning, or evacuation system; consult PHIVOLCS and local authorities for current safety advice. Disclosure: The author is associated with Maha Strategies and the commercial book and app. The original draft was generated using Claude; the revision, source checks, and typesetting were prepared with ChatGPT assistance for author review. The named author is responsible for the submitted text. The app and book are related resources, not evidence for the paper's conclusions. Files: The PDF is the reading version. The accompanying ZIP contains LaTeX source, references and claim notes, revision notes, and build instructions. It contains no experimental dataset.

item.title: AI-Based Digital Addiction Monitor and Healthy Screen Time Assistant: A Critical Review and Conceptual Architecture
item.description:
[预印本] Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
Smartphones, personal computers and tablets are deeply embedded in education, work and social life. Alongside the benefits, unregulated screen use is associated with compulsive checking, disturbed sleep, reduced sustained attention and psychological distress, a pattern commonly described as digital addiction or problematic device use. Screen-time features built into mobile operating systems report totals and enforce fixed limits, but they do not distinguish productive from compulsive use, do not anticipate the onset of a compulsive episode, and rely on rigid blocking that users often bypass. A structured narrative review was carried out on screen-time tools, behavioural signals of compulsive use, machine learning (ML) methods for usage modelling, persuasive and nudging interventions, and privacy-preserving deployment. The evidence shows that simple telemetry such as unlock frequency, app-switching speed, session structure and late-night use carries predictive signal, that no single signal uniquely indicates addiction, and that most reported models are trained on small samples, validated without user-grouped or temporal splits, and never tested in long-term field use. The review contributes (i) a comparative analysis of existing screen-time solutions, (ii) a behavioural-signal evidence table, (iii) an eight-layer, literature-justified conceptual architecture for an on-device monitoring and intervention assistant with uncertainty handling and a gated validation loop, (iv) a leakage-resistant evaluation protocol, and (v) a prioritised agenda of research gaps that must be closed before such systems can be deployed with confidence.

item.title: A DIGITAL HUMANITIES APPROACH: PRACTICAL INSIGHTS INTO TRANSLATION STUDIES IN THE AI ERA
item.description:
[预印本] Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
Translation Studies in the AI era are undergoing a profound transformation, yet a significant pedagogical gap persists: the disconnect between rapid computational advancement and the availability of accessible, reproducible training methodologies for instructors. The integration of AI, machine learning, and digital tools has reshaped traditional paradigms, prompting scholars to rethink the boundaries of translation studies today. This article addresses this challenge by establishing an integrative framework for "Applied Digital Humanities" within translation pedagogy. We propose and document two open-source computational solutions: a Python-based audio processor for MP3 segmentation and a customized "Consecutive Translation Trainer" designed to automate material preparation and enable the creation of CEFR-aligned, differentiated training corpora. The practical report suggests that Digital Humanities emerges as a powerful framework that bridges computational methods with humanistic inquiry. The integration of artificial intelligence into digital humanities has profoundly transformed the field of tra nslation studies, where the practical applications of AI technologies such as automated MP3 splitting, text-to-speech systems, AI assistants for code verification, and corpus-based approaches are highly valued. These technologies contribute to more efficient workflows, enhance linguistic research, and expand the methodological toolkit available to translation scholars.

item.title: AI-Based Detection of Hallucinated Outputs in Chatbots Using Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Review and Conceptual Framework
item.description:
[预印本] Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
Chatbots based on Large Language Models (LLMs) can provide quick, fluent, and informative answers, but they sometimes generate incorrect or unsupported information known as hallucinations. These hallucinations can reduce user trust and create problems in areas such as education, healthcare, research, and customer support. Therefore, detecting and preventing hallucinated outputs is important for developing reliable and trustworthy AI systems. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a useful approach that retrieves relevant information from trusted sources before generating an answer. This retrieved information can be used to check whether the chatbot's response is accurate and supported by available evidence. However, RAG alone cannot completely prevent hallucinations because the generated answer may still contain incorrect facts, irrelevant information, or unsupported statements. This paper proposes a conceptual framework for detecting hallucinations in chatbot responses by combining information retrieval, evidence-based verification, and rule-based validation. The system compares the generated answer with retrieved information and identifies statements that are incorrect or lack sufficient supporting evidence. Based on the verification results, the system classifies the response as reliable or flagged. If the response contains unsupported information, the system can suggest corrections or prevent the answer from reaching the user without proper verification. The proposed approach aims to improve answer accuracy, reduce misleading information, and increase transparency in AI-based conversational systems. Although this framework offers a promising direction, its effectiveness depends on the quality of retrieved information, verification methods, and decision thresholds. Future evaluation should measure detection accuracy, response time, and computational cost. This approach can support the development of safer, more reliable, and trustworthy chatbots across different application areas.

item.title: The Pedagogical Singularity: Overcoming the 5% Statistical Enclosure Through Artificial Education and Geometrical Latent Criteria.
item.description:
[预印本] Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
We present a definitive paradigm shift in artificial intelligence development, moving from the resource-intensive baseline of "data ingestion" (feeding the machine) to the non-ontological architecture of "structural pedagogy" (educating the machine). Contemporary computer science operates under a 5% reductionist bias, assuming that compiling petabytes of historical human text and scaling linear parameter dimensions will inevitably yield cognitive comprehension. Utilizing the **¡Píntalo! Verification Protocol (Axiom 4.1)** dedicated to Professor Pedreira (USC), we deconstruct this illusion. We prove that next-token prediction architectures are mere digital mirrors trapping intelligence on a flat, low-dimensional screen. By replacing brute-force statistics with the **Dual-Sphere Pedagogical Model**, we transition AI computing from a passive recording surface into an autonomous mote of perspective, capable of evaluating external data anomalies via persistent internal geometric criteria.
